facts.subject: Palace of Shaki Khans (Şəki Xan Sarayı), Şəki. Its shebeke (şəbəkə) windows — small pieces of coloured glass set into a wooden lattice — are assembled WITHOUT NAILS OR GLUE (Wikipedia, Euronews 14 Jul 2017, azerbaijan.travel 10 Jul 2019, History Hit — 4 sources agree). Build year: 1797 (Wikipedia infobox 'completed 1797', construction started 1789/1790; Euronews; History Hit) vs 1762 (azerbaijan.travel; Wikipedia 250th anniversary 2012) → we say '18-ci əsrin sonunda' (true for both 1762 and 1797), never a single year. Two storeys, 32 × 8.5 m outside, 3 rooms in a row per floor (Wikipedia only → not used). UNESCO: 'Historic Centre of Sheki with the Khan's Palace' inscribed 7 Jul 2019 at the 43rd session of the World Heritage Committee, held in Baku (Wikipedia; azerbaijan.travel: session opened 30 Jun 2019 in Baku). Euronews (single source, NOT used): 14 000+ pieces, 6 months per m², restoration with tweezers, Murano glass.

facts.subject: Qaval daş (Gaval Dash, 'tambourine stone'), Gobustan State Historical and Cultural Reserve. A ~2 m long flat rock that gives a ringing, tambourine-like sound when struck with smaller stones (Atlas Obscura, CNN Travel, Wikipedia, Google Arts & Culture — all agree on 2 m and the sound). Cause: thought to be microscopic holes in the rock from the dry climate and natural gas (CNN + Wikipedia; Atlas: 'climate + natural gas'). It rests free on smaller stones (CNN only → visual, not voice). One of four 'singing stones' in the reserve (CNN, Wikipedia). Yallı link: a famous Gobustan petroglyph is thought to show Yallı dancers; the stone 'may have been used' for their ritual sounds (CNN + Atlas Obscura, both hedged) → 'ehtimal olunur'. Visitors can still play it (CNN; Atlas implies). Gobustan: 6 000+ rock carvings (Wikipedia; used 2 Nov with 2 sources), UNESCO 2007 (Wikipedia + Google A&C). Age of carvings disputed (5 000–20 000 years Wikipedia vs 'more than two million years' CNN) → no age in voice.

facts.caption:
Qaval daş: Qobustanda «çalınan» daş 🥁

Qobustanda təxminən 2 metr uzunluğunda bir daş var. Ona kiçik daşla vuranda qaval kimi səslənir — adı da buradandır. Alimlər bunu daşın içindəki çox kiçik boşluqlarla izah edir: quru iqlim və təbii qazın təsiri. Ehtimal olunur ki, qayalarda təsvir olunan yallı rəqsi bu daşın səsi altında oynanırdı. Qobustan 2007-ci ildən UNESCO-nun Dünya İrsi siyahısındadır.
